source.title: Multiple Descent: Design Your Own Generalization Curve
source.authors: Lin Chen; Yi-Fei Min; Mikhail Belkin; Amin Karbasi

record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically measures how changing feature dimension changes expected test risk in linear regression, using a different model and constructed feature distributions. It does not test the listed deep-network or natural-label settings.
record.gate_note: The study's own theoretical results measure changes in excess generalization loss as features are revealed. The paper also cites empirical neural-network results in prior work; those cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves results about feature dimension and expected squared prediction loss in least-squares linear regression. It does not test any listed version. In particular, adding constructed features to a linear regressor does not test V2's widening of ReLU networks on image classification.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors prove that constructed feature-revealing processes permit multiple descents and prescribed ascents and descents in overparameterized linear regression. They argue that typical generalization curves reflect interactions between data properties and algorithmic inductive biases. Arbitrary curve control concerns directions of change away from interpolation, not arbitrary numerical risk values; underparameterized risk is nondecreasing.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical least-squares linear regression with a minimum-norm solution in the overparametrized regime; features are revealed according to deliberately constructed Gaussian or Gaussian-mixture distributions. No neural-network training recipe is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction of the risk change depends on the distribution of the newly revealed feature; feature order can change the curve. In the Gaussian-coefficient setting, the stated Gaussian-feature decrease also depends on the bound on ρ.

fits_no_version.finding: In the paper's underparameterized regression setup, expected excess loss cannot decrease when a feature is added, and suitable mixture features permit arbitrarily large increases. Beyond d = n + 8, constructed feature distributions can realize any finite prescribed sequence of risk increases and decreases, both for zero coefficients and for suitably scaled Gaussian coefficients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For minimum-norm least-squares regression with fixed sample size, constructed feature distributions can produce arbitrary sequences of risk-change directions sufficiently beyond interpolation; increasing dimension need not monotonically improve generalization.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and concern linear regression under constructed feature distributions. They do not establish behavior on natural data or in deep neural networks.
record.rows_left_out: No study results that meet the row criteria were left out. Cited results from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Natural-label versus random-label fitting and held-out classification accuracy.
Test error as ReLU networks widen beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers under different tuning recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus random training examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The row states indicate inability to assess a listed claim version, not uncertainty about the stated theoretical results. The constructions do not challenge V2 within its specified neural-network setting.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels.
Does not study one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or widening networks trained by gradient methods; its model is linear regression with a constructed feature-revealing process.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks.
Does not compare batch sizes or training recipes.
Does not study dropout or weight decay.
Does not measure sharpness or other trained-network properties against a generalization gap.
Does not remove or retrain on memorized examples.

rows.subject: Least square linear regression, underparametrized regime
rows.size_stated: Feature dimension d < n; sample size n not specified
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically compare excess generalization loss as feature dimension increases by one, for arbitrary data distributions.
rows.note: The theorem states non-decrease for the underparametrized regime, regardless of data distribution.
rows.check: Theorem 1 establishes nondecreasing risk in the paper's underparameterized regression setup; this does not measure any listed version. The recorded inequality is correct.

rows.subject: Least square linear regression, underparametrized regime
rows.size_stated: Feature dimension d < n; sample size n not specified
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically add a feature drawn from a trimodal Gaussian mixture.
rows.measure: Change in expected excess generalization loss, L_{d+1} − L_d
rows.value: For any C > 0, there exists a distribution D such that L_{d+1} − L_d > C
rows.note: The result establishes an arbitrarily large increase for a suitable mixture feature distribution.
rows.check: Theorem 4 establishes an arbitrarily large increase by choosing the added mixture feature's variance, assuming finite initial loss. This is a constructed linear-regression result outside the listed versions.

rows.subject: Least square linear regression, overparametrized regime, β = 0
rows.size_stated: Feature dimension d ≥ n + 8; n < D − 9
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically add a Gaussian or Gaussian mixture feature to control the change in expected excess generalization loss.

conditions.value: Gaussian N(0, σ²) for a decrease; Gaussian mixture N^{mix}_{σ,μ} for an increase

rows.measure: Expected excess generalization loss L_d as feature dimension increases
rows.value: For any specified sequence of increases and decreases over dimensions d ≥ n + 8, there exists a distribution D realizing it
rows.note: This is a theoretical construction with a feature distribution chosen to realize the specified direction at each step.
rows.check: Theorem 5 establishes prescribed directions of risk changes for constructed minimum-norm linear regressors. Gaussian-feature decreases require a suitably chosen variance and the stated moment conditions; they are not guaranteed for arbitrary Gaussian features.

rows.subject: Least square linear regression, overparametrized regime, β ∼ N(0, ρ²)
rows.size_stated: Feature dimension d ≥ n + 8; n < D − 9
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically add a Gaussian or Gaussian mixture feature to control the change in expected risk averaged over β.

conditions.value: Gaussian mixture for an increase; Gaussian for a decrease under the stated bound on ρ

rows.measure: Expected risk L_d^{exp} as feature dimension increases
rows.value: For any specified sequence of increases and decreases over dimensions d ≥ n + 8, there exist ρ and D realizing it
rows.note: The Gaussian-feature decrease is subject to the theorem's stated bound on ρ.
rows.check: Theorem 11 establishes prescribed risk-change directions with a jointly chosen feature distribution and coefficient scale. Each coefficient is independently Gaussian, equivalently β ∼ N(0, ρ²I_d); decreases require the stated bound on ρ. No listed version is measured.
